title: Why Post-starburst Galaxies Are Now Quiescent
question: Do CO-luminous but quiescent post-starburst galaxies contain dense gas (HCN, HCO+), and does a lack of dense gas explain their low star formation rates?

data.arrays: 12m array; 43 antennas for H02, 41-46 for S05
data.sensitivity: H02 HCN 5.5 mJy/beam, HCO+ 2.7 mJy/beam; S05 570 uJy/beam both

what.value: CO (1-0) luminosities and CO linewidths of H02 and S05
TIR, [CII] and [NeII]+[NeIII] SFRs and dust masses

evidence.quote: S05 has a TIR SFR consistent with the other measures from the optical and radio, at 0.71 M$_\ensuremath{\odot}$yr$^{-1}$

what.value: HCN and CO comparison samples of star-forming and early-type galaxies

evidence.quote: comparison samples of star-forming and early type galaxies with both HCN and CO measurements (cite: Gao2004; Crocker2012)
The comparison samples of star-forming and starbursting galaxies are from (cite: Gracia2008)
For the early type galaxies, SFRs are from (cite: Davis2014)

recipe.goal: Image cubes and check for HCN/HCO+ detections
recipe.method: Pipeline-calibrated data imaged; no lines detected; tests with 5 arcsec taper and matched filter

recipe.goal: Compute 3 sigma line luminosity upper limits
recipe.method: L' = 3.25e7 (1+z)^-3 nu_obs^-2 S dv D_L^2 integrated over CO (1-0) linewidth
Compare SFRs from Halpha, Dn4000, FIRST 1.4 GHz and infrared tracers; adopt SFR <1 Msun/yr for H02

recipe.goal: Compare with L'-SFR relations and HCN/CO ratios of comparison samples
recipe.method: Monte-Carlo drawing pairs of galaxies from comparison samples to assess probability of ratios as low as post-starbursts
assumptions: Early-type conversion from main beam temperature to flux density 4.73 Jy/K

recipe.method: DESPOTIC models of alpha_CO and alpha_HCN for MW GMC and ULIRG conditions
assumptions: Same HCN-to-dense gas conversion for post-starbursts and other galaxies

answer_key.quantity: Probability two galaxies from combined comparison sample have HCN/CO as low as post-starbursts

evidence.quote: the probability of finding two galaxies with HCN/CO as low as the post-starbursts is 5%
we find that two galaxies have HCN/CO luminosity ratios as low as the two post-starbursts 16% of the time
we find two galaxies with HCN/CO as low as the post-starbursts only 2% of the time

answer_key.quantity: alpha_CO ULIRG vs MW GMC ratio from DESPOTIC

evidence.loc: 4.3 Variations in luminosity to mass conversion
evidence.quote: However, $\alpha_{\rm HCN}$ is lowered by the same factor.

not_stated_but_needed: Imaging task, weighting/robust, cell and image size, and cleaning parameters
How the 3 sigma upper limits and noise were computed (channel width, integration window)
Monte Carlo procedure details (sample selection, draws, definition of 'as low as')
score_reason: Simple non-detection analysis and archive data, but imaging and Monte Carlo details are missing.
rediscovery_reason: Public ALMA data, simple recipe, numeric upper limits, though imaging details need to be inferred.
